requirements.raw_text: Select from List of Courses: 6 units

courses.title: Python for Beginners
courses.requirement: Minor Required: 18 units
courses.description: Basic concepts of computer software and programming. Numbers, strings, and basic I/O. Expressions, control structures, lists, tuples, and functions. File I/O and introduction to exception handling. Introduction to object-oriented programming. Problem-solving techniques. Cannot be used for CS elective credit.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 or MAT 1052 .

courses.title: Python for Programmers
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: Python basics. Data structures and control structures. Functions and functional forms. Objects, classes, inheritance, and polymorphism. I/O and exceptions. Advanced features.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 1400 or CS 1280 ; Data Science minor, AI Minor or Computational Linguistics Minor and C or better in MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , or MAT 1140 ; or Cyber Security minor and C or better in CS 1400 .

courses.title: Fundamentals of Data Science
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: Foundations of data science. Critical concepts and skills in mathematics, statistics and computer programming for data analytics. Fundamental data and file structures to support data analytics. Analysis of real-world datasets. Data privacy and data security.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 1400 , or Data Science/ AI/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 1260 ; MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , or MAT 1140 ; and STA 1200 , STA 1202 , STA 1300 , STA 2100 , or STA 2260 .

courses.title: Introduction to English Linguistics
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: [GE 3B] The study of English as a science and a cultural phenomenon. Exploration of fundamental properties of English and of ways in which English differs from other languages. Topics include the sounds, word formation and meaning, syntax, history, and dialects of English.

courses.title: Applied Language Studies Capstone Seminar
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: Research project examining how key issues and theories in applied language studies shape developments in various professional, industrial, and social fields. Application of the descriptive, analytical, and professional writing skills gained in the program. Culmination of fully-developed research paper and presentation. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing, and BA in English - Applied Linguistics Option or Computational Linguistics minor; or instructor permission.

courses.title: College Algebra
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: [GE 2] The theory and applications of real-valued functions, domain and range, compositions, inverses, transformations, equations and inequalities, and absolute value. Emphasis on polynomials, rational functions, power and root functions, piecewise functions, logarithms and exponential functions. Both symbolic and graphical representations of functions. Use of graphing devices to support reasoning about functions.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, or C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course.

courses.title: College Algebra Stretch II
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: [GE 2] This is the second of a two course sequence in College Algebra. The theory and applications of real-valued functions. Graphing and solving equations with exponential and logarithmic functions. Equations and inequalities, including polynomial and absolutely value inequalities. Systems of equations, both linear and nonlinear. Symbolic and graphical representations of functions. Use of graphing devices to support reasoning about functions.
courses.prerequisites: CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Statistics with Applications
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: [GE 2] Sample and population data; descriptive statistics, including numerical and graphical summarization of central tendency and spread; elementary probability, including events, basic probability rules, binomial and normal distributions; inferential statistics, including confidence intervals and hypothesis tests for one-population mean and proportion problems, simple linear regression and correlation
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, ALEKS >=46, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Statistics with Applications Stretch II
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: [GE 2] This is the second semester of two in the Statistics with Applications stretch sequence that introduces the concepts of probability and basic descriptive statistics with requisite arithmetic and algebraic topics integrated throughout. This path is designed to serve students with majors that require no college-level mathematics beyond introductory freshman-level statistics. Students must take a year-long sequence to receive credit for college-level statistics. STA 1202 is focused mainly on the elementary probability theory and statistical inference. STA 1201 is a prerequisite for STA 1202. STA 1201 and STA 1202 together are equivalent to STA 1200. This sequence covers topics that include basic concepts of probability, discrete and continuous random variables, sampling distributions, introduction to statistical inference, confidence intervals for population means and proportions, hypothesis testing for population means and proportions, and correlation and regression model.
courses.prerequisites: CR in STA 1201 or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Biostatistics
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: [GE 2] Basic definitions, Sampling methods, Graphical display and descriptive statistics. Probability concepts, Normal distribution. Estimation, hypothesis testing, t-tests, goodness of fit, analysis of variance, regression and correlation, and nonparametric procedures. Applications in biological, agricultural, and other applied science. Use of computer packages for applied problems.
courses.prerequisites: Category I, Category II, MDPT >=14, ALEKS >=46, SAT >=570, ACT >=23, C or better in a GE Sub-area 2/B4 course, or C- or better or CR in MAT 1051 .

courses.title: Introduction to Statistics
courses.requirement: or
courses.description: Population and sample data; random sampling; numerical and graphical summarization of data; basic probability concepts, including binomial and normal distributions; sampling distributions and the central limit theorem; point estimates, confidence intervals, and hypothesis tests for one- and two-sample mean and proportion problems; contingency tables and chi-squared tests; simple linear regression and correlation; one-way ANOVA; illustration with statistical software packages used throughout.
courses.prerequisites: AP Calc AB, AP Calc BC, MAT 1140 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1150 , or MAT 2140 .

courses.title: Natural Language Processing
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: Introduction to natural language processing with emphasis on foundational methods. Topics include lexical, syntactic, and basic semantic analysis; statistical algorithms and classical machine learning models for language representation and modeling; introductory word embeddings and applied use of NLP libraries. Case studies include sentiment analysis, text classification, and chatbots.
courses.prerequisites: Computer Science major and CS 3010 ; or Data Science, Computational Linguistics, or Artificial Intelligence minor and C or better in CS 2410 .

courses.title: Artificial Intelligence
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: Overview of the different application areas of AI. Introduction to the basic AI concepts and techniques such as heuristic search, knowledge representation, automated reasoning. In-depth discussion of several AI application areas: their specific problems, tools and techniques.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; or Data Science/ AI/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 .

courses.title: Machine Learning and Its Applications
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: Supervised learning techniques, including linear models for regression, linear models for classification, decision trees, support vector machines, neural networks. Unsupervised learning techniques, including clustering and dimensionality reduction. Related advanced topics. Case studies and applications.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 3010 ; Data Science minor/ AI/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; Cybersecurity minor and C or better in CS 2400 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Web Search and Recommender Systems
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: Web Search engine architectures, techniques, and technologies. Web crawling. Web document processing, Link analysis, and ranking. Introduction to retrieval models. Search engine optimization. Web search user interfaces. Recommender Systems. Evaluation. Current trends.
courses.prerequisites: CS major or CS minor, and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science/ Artificial Intelligence/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Data Mining
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: An end-to-end view of data mining, covering data acquisition, preparation, and analysis using various algorithms. Explore data types, attributes, storage, and perform exploratory data analysis with statistical techniques and visualization. Topics include pattern mining, clustering, classification, and outlier detection. Ethical considerations and applications of data mining are also discussed.
courses.prerequisites: CS major and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science/ ArtificiaI Intelligence/ Computational Linguistics minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Prompt Engineering
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: A comprehensive introduction to prompt engineering, focusing on designing effective prompts for Large Language Models (LLMs). Students will explore essential concepts, including LLM foundations, interactive prompts, and parameter tuning. Various prompt patterns and templates, customization and fine-tuning techniques, and methods for evaluating prompt effectiveness are covered. Ethical considerations and security aspects in prompt engineering will also be discussed. Additionally, learn to apply prompt engineering in specialized domains through hands-on development, gaining practical experience in building AI-powered applications.
courses.prerequisites: CS major/ CS minor/ Cybersecurity minor and C or better in CS 2400 ; Data Science/ Computational Linguistic/ AI minor and C or better in CS 2410 ; or consent of instructor.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Syntax
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: Introduction to the structure and organization of human languages. Syntactic analysis using data from English and other languages. Exploration of the fundamentals of syntactic theory. Development of skills in linguistic problem-solving, logical argumentation, and representation of language structure.
courses.prerequisites: ENG 214 or ENG 2200 .

courses.title: Language Acquisition
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: Development of first language from birth through adolescence. Adult and child acquisition of second and subsequent languages. Linguistic, biological, and social factors that facilitate and hinder language learning. Theoretical and practical applications.
courses.prerequisites: Completion of GE Area 1B or A3.

courses.title: Analysis of Conversation
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: Study of sequences of spoken utterances. Emphasis on linguistic and interactional characteristics of conversation, with comparisons of conversational practices across cultures
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing, senior standing, or ENG 2200 .

courses.title: Applied Pragmatics
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: Study of relationship between linguistic forms and their uses within a context. Focus on forms involved in deixis, speech acts, implicature, and politeness theory. Emphasis on practical applications in the business world and the language classroom.
courses.prerequisites: Junior standing, senior standing, or completion of GE Area 1A/A2; and ENG 2200 or ENG 214.

courses.title: Applied Phonology
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: Specialized instruction on English phonology. Introduction to the sound system, IPA, articulatory phonetics, and phonological processes. Computer training provided for speech analyses. Applications of phonology to real-world contexts. Course culminates in research topic of student’s choice.

courses.title: Digital Analysis of Texts
courses.requirement: Select from List of Courses: 6 units
courses.description: Digital analysis of language used in authentic texts such as news articles, social media posts, speeches, songs, and literature. Build text datasets to identify language patterns, themes, and implicit meanings. Emphasis on the design and presentation of a research project.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing. Completion of GE Areas 1A, 1B, 1C, and 2 is recommended.
